sections.h2: Selling a Cedar Hill house for cash
sections.html:
Cedar Hill sellers can list with an agent, run their own sale, or take cash. A cash buyer needs no lender and can often close sooner, though the price already accounts for repairs and risk. Request every offer in writing, including title costs and what an inspection could change.

The condition of the house points toward an answer. A tidy home on a quiet street may bring more as a listing, while one carrying deferred repairs, tenants or tax trouble may fit a direct sale better. Weigh what you would take home each way once costs and waiting are subtracted, and ask every buyer how long closing will take and who pays for title work.

A sale by owner falls in the middle. You save the commission but take on the contract, the buyer screening and the paperwork, and the title company asks for the same documents in every case.

sections.h2: Cedar Hill's hills, lake and buyers
sections.html:
Cedar Hill sits about 18 miles southwest of downtown Dallas along US Highway 67, mostly in Dallas County with small parts in Ellis County. Joe Pool Lake lies along its western edge, with Cedar Hill State Park beside it. The Balcones Escarpment runs through town, so many lots slope, and Red Oak Creek and Bentle Branch Creek cross it. Drainage, foundation movement and flood questions come up often, so keep surveys and repair records ready.

Buyers tend to want hills, water and a short drive to the metroplex. Downtown Fort Worth is 30 miles away and DFW Airport 27 miles. Lead with the lake and park when you describe the house, and be ready to document any yard drainage or retaining work on a sloped lot.

Growth came late to Cedar Hill. The population was 2,160 in 1970, 6,847 in 1980 and 20,267 in 1990, a jump tied to Joe Pool Dam, completed in 1985, and the lake behind it. Many houses therefore date from the 1980s or later. Roofs, HVAC systems and original windows from that period may be near the end of their life, and buyers will price that in. If you plan to list, a quick check of the roof, the air conditioning and the windows tells you what to expect before a buyer's inspector does. If you plan to sell as-is for cash, just tell the buyer what you know about each system and its age.

Landlords have to register. The City Council passed a Single Family Rental Registration Ordinance on November 10, 2020, and enforcement began January 1, 2021. Single family rentals, duplexes and townhomes included, must be registered every year and again when ownership changes. A tenant-occupied sale should come with proof that the registration is current.

Each tenant change calls for a new certificate of occupancy, and a code officer inspects the exterior within 30 days. Code Enforcement is at the Government Center, 285 Uptown Boulevard, and takes email at code@cedarhilltx.com.

For school taxes, $140,000 of a homestead is exempt, and an owner aged 65 or over or disabled gets $60,000 on top. Local governments can also offer an option of up to 20 percent of value. The county tax office can tell you whether Cedar Hill's units use it.

  • A senior or disabled homestead's school tax is frozen at the level of the first qualifying year.
  • If you buy again, the ceiling can move in proportion to a new Texas homestead.
  • A disabled veteran's exemption grows with the rating, and 100 percent means a full exemption on the homestead.
  • If the seller never held the exemption, a buyer after January 1 may claim it for that year.

Tell your agent if a freeze applies to your house. The buyer does not inherit it.

sections.h2: Contract for deed, Lady Bird deed and heirs
sections.html:
If a buyer lives in the home under a contract for deed, sometimes called a lease to own, Property Code chapter 5, subchapter D applies. The seller keeps title until payment is finished. State law gives the buyer a right to cancel, with notice periods spelled out in the code. Anyone holding one should ask a lawyer how it changes a sale.

A transfer on death deed filed before the owner dies sends the property to the beneficiary without probate. A Lady Bird deed lets the owner sell without asking the named beneficiary. Heirs with neither deed may need a muniment of title or a small estate affidavit to move the deed.

sections.h2: Removing an occupant before you sell
sections.html:
Start with the right notice. The written notice to vacate usually gives three days. Hand it to the tenant or to a household member aged 16 or older, post it inside the home where it can be seen, or mail it. Email works only when the written lease permits it.

  • The case is heard in justice court, and the tenant must be served at least four days before trial.
  • Expect the hearing 10 to 21 days after the filing date.
  • Appealing to county court has to happen within five days of judgment.
  • A writ can be requested six days after final judgment, and removal follows 24 hours' notice.

A person who stays after being told to leave, with no lease and no family tie, might be removed on a sheriff's or constable's request under Property Code chapter 24B, with no court case. A wrongful removal invites a lawsuit, so talk to the sheriff's or constable's office before acting.

sections.h2: Documents for a sloped or creek-side lot
sections.html:
Water shows up in buyer conversations here. If the lot slopes toward the house, backs onto a creek or has a retaining wall, write down what was done and when. Keep the survey, any engineer's letter and invoices for foundation or drainage work in one folder. If you have never had a problem, say that too, and note how long you have lived there. Buyers and their inspectors are far more comfortable with a seller who can show records than one who shrugs.

On the cash side, an investor will inspect the same things and subtract the cost of anything unresolved. Records can narrow that gap, because they replace guesses with facts.

Gather the tax statement, a payoff letter if a loan exists, the rental registration and certificate of occupancy if a tenant lives there, and any survey or drainage and foundation repair records. A buyer given those on day one can price faster, and the title company can see who needs to sign.

faqs.q: Is Cedar Hill in Dallas County or Ellis County?
faqs.a: Most of it is in Dallas County, and a small part is in Ellis County. Check your tax bill for the county, which fixes your clerk and appraisal district.

faqs.q: How much does Cedar Hill charge to register a rental?
faqs.a: The city lists $50 for the first annual registration or a change of owner, $25 to renew and $75 for a late renewal. A Residential Rental Certificate of Occupancy costs $25 at each tenant change. Confirm current fees with Code Enforcement.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cedar Hill house with a tenant?
faqs.a: Yes, and the buyer takes the house subject to the lease unless it ends first. Keep the rental registration current. A new certificate of occupancy will be required for the next tenant.

faqs.q: What is the school homestead exemption near Cedar Hill?
faqs.a: School districts exempt $140,000 by state rule, with $60,000 more for qualifying seniors and disabled owners. It follows the owner who lives in the house, so each buyer applies separately.

faqs.q: Can a Lady Bird deed help me sell?
faqs.a: It can. The owner stays free to sell or mortgage, and at death the home passes outside probate. No official form exists in Texas, so work with a lawyer or the county clerk's guidance.
